title: Cohort-based VPC Upgrade Orchestrator and Rollout Gate Framework
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Design and implement a cohort-based upgrade orchestrator for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). Goal is to provide a safe, automated path to perform multi-stage upgrades (control plane + agents + schema migrations) with gates at each cohort, integrated preflight checks, and explicit rollback semantics. This ticket covers the orchestration state machine, cohort selection logic, gating policies (health, compatibility, latency), and an audit trail for compliance. The system must support dry-runs, staged DB migrations (transactional when possible), and a canary->small->broad cohort expansion pattern.

This work is distinct from previous 'migration runner' tickets: instead of focusing on the migration implementation, we are building the coordinator that schedules and enforces rollout gates across customer cohorts, including support for manual interventions, automated rollbacks, and policy-driven escalation to dedicated capacity or alternative model variants for critical customers.
acceptance_criteria:
- Orchestrator can define a rollout plan consisting of named cohorts (canary, alpha, beta, general) and progress through them automatically when gates pass.
- Preflight checks (version compatibility, agent heartbeat, disk space, KMS access) are executed and results stored in the audit trail.
- Gates include: service health, error-rate delta threshold, CPU/GPU load thresholds, and critical customer smoke tests.
- Dry-run mode performs all checks and simulates cohort transitions without changing live state.
- Rollback action reverses agent configuration and allows schema rollback where the migration is reversible; rollback events are recorded with timestamps and owners.
- Exposes a minimal API for Console to show cohort status, recent gate events, and to trigger manual advance or rollback.
- Integration tests (end-to-end on staging) exercising canary failure -> automatic rollback and canary success -> expand to next cohort pass.
technical_notes:
Architecture: coordinator service will be an independent control-plane microservice (upgrade-orchestrator) that persists plans and state to Jobs DB and emits events to Kafka for execution agents.

State machine: INITIAL -> PRECHECK -> CANARY -> WAIT_GATES -> EXPAND -> FINALIZE -> ROLLING_BACK -> ABORTED. Each transition evaluated by gate evaluators.

Gate evaluators: pluggable components that run health queries against Prometheus, call the private console smoke-test endpoint, and validate DB migration diffs. They must be idempotent and return structured pass/fail + tolerances.

Cohort selection: support static lists, label selectors (customer tier, region), and dynamic sampling (n% traffic). Cohorts must be deterministic and checkpointed.

Migrations: where possible use transactional schema changes and feature flags. For non-transactional steps (e.g., backfill), orchestrator will create sub-jobs with resumable checkpoints and can throttle concurrency.

Security: all upgrade commands signed with a key tied to the release pipeline; orchestrator must verify KMS access to customer KMS before any key rotations. Audit log retains payloads for 90 days by default (configurable).
rollout_plan:
1) Create rollout plan from release pipeline (release-2026.04) with cohorts: canary(1 cluster), early(5%), regional-beta(20%), GA(100%).
2) PRECHECK phase runs preflight pipelines: config lint, agent compatibility, disk-health, KMS connectivity.
3) If prechecks pass, move to CANARY: schedule control-plane upgrade and agent v2 on canary cluster. Trigger smoke tests and collect metrics for 30m.
4) WAIT_GATES: evaluate gates. If pass, EXPAND to next cohort. If fail, either HALT (manual decision) or ROLLING_BACK depending on policy.
5) FINALIZE once GA cohort completes and post-upgrade validation passes.

Policies: default auto-expand on green for canary->early, but require manual approval for early->regional-beta when critical customers present. These overrides configurable in plan metadata.
migration_playbook:
- Pre-upgrade: take control-plane snapshot, export schema diff, notify customers in planned cohort window.
- During: run preflight checks, start agent upgrades with max parallelism = 5 clusters, run smoke tests, monitor for 15-60 minutes per cohort.
- Schema changes: if change is non-destructive, apply in single transaction; if destructive, run dual-write adapter then backfill and switch.
- Rollback: revert agent binary via orchestration agent, restore control-plane snapshot if persistent state corruption detected; for schema rollbacks use reverse migration provided by migration factory when available.
- Post-upgrade: run regression evals (critical prompts), confirm latency within SLO, mark release as complete and emit audit entry.
